name: Separate permission authority
note: Policy service apart from the agent
summary: Permission decisions live in a service outside the agent process. The agent asks the authority whether an action is allowed; the authority applies central policy, returns allow, deny or escalate, and records the decision, so a compromised or confused agent can't grant itself access.
how: Agent sends the intended action and context to the policy service
Service evaluates who is asking, what action, on which system
It allows, denies, or escalates to a human
facts: WorkOS Airlock (preview, Oct 2026); Auth0 asynchronous authorization (CIBA)
Claude Code: permission rules are enforced by the harness, not the model
Stronger isolation and one place for policy, but another service to run and a network hop per action
goodFor: Companies running many agents under one policy
Regulated environments that need a decision log
watchOut: Policy service becomes a single point of failure
Coarse policies push everything into escalation
